newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL CLINCH SPANISH TITLE IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-REAL CLINCH SPANISH TITLE IN STYLE.

text.p: Real Madrid won their 27th Spanish league title in fine style on Saturday with an impressive 3-1 victory over reigning champions Atletico.
Needing just a point, Real tore their neighbours apart with first half goals from Raul Gonzalez and Fernando Hierro. Predrag Mijatovic added the third shortly after the break.
Atletico coach Radomir Antic made a triple-substitution after Mijatovic's goal and was quickly rewarded with a goal from former Real striker Juan Eduardo Esnaider.
Real weathered 10 minutes of heavy pressure before running out easy winners.
"I dedicate the title to my wife," said Capello.
"We were leaders for a long time, and that has a lot of merit," he said.
Capello has already announced that he will not continue at the club next season.
Real president Lorenzo Sanz took the opportunity to announce that Tenerife coach Jupp Heynckes will almost certainly be the next man to occupy the hot seat at the Bernabeu stadium.
"We have the basis of an agreement with Heynckes. I don't think there will be any problem," said Sanz, who was close to tears.
Real never looked troubled by the absence of dynamic Brazilian left-back Roberto Carlos, and Atletico keeper Jose Molina was quickly stretched by efforts from Manolo Sanchis and Mijatovic.
But Molina stood no chance of saving Gonzalez's 36th minute strike.

The teenager -- who earlier in the season had played the game of his life against Atletico -- controlled a difficult cross from the left and worked his way into position before unleashing a powerful shot into the net.
Just before half-time Real went two-up when Molina was left standing by a free-kick from Hierro that caught a deflection.
Real refused to rest on their laurels and came out looking for more after the break.
The game was sealed in the 56th minute when Clarence Seedorf sliced open a sleepy Atletico defence before feeding the ball to Mijatovic to score.
Antic's tactical change seemed -- at least momentarily -- to galvanise his side into action.
Real keeper Bodo Illgner forced a long-range lob from Kiko Narvaez against the post and moments later another slip left Esnaider unmarked with only Illgner to beat.
Antic was full of praise for his opponents.
"We can't call it luck, it was quality, they've got some great players," he said.
"You win championships with regularity throughout the year, and in that category Real were the best side," he said.
Within minutes of the final whistle tens of thousands of Real fans had already converged on Cibeles, the fountain where supporters traditionally celebrate their side's victories.
